test_cases._note_for_reviewer: The doc's core regression claim is that ped_latched[0] survives the mid-FDW re-press (only ped_recall[0] is cleared, not ped_latched[0]), so a brand-new WALK/FDW/DONT_WALK sequence for side 0 auto-starts at the NEXT ARTERIAL_GREEN (~t=90000ms) with no further keypress. This tool's checks match the FIRST occurrence of a pattern with timestamp>=t0 in the transcript, so a fourth check for a second 'PED SIGNAL side 0 -> WALK' at ~90000ms would trivially be satisfied by the FIRST WALK at t~=300ms already (both lines are textually identical) and would NOT actually prove the second occurrence happened - this is a structural limitation of the runner's single-pattern-match check model, not something expressible with the current schema. cleanup_wait_ms is extended to 92000ms so a human reviewing results/TC-SC02-5/L1.log after the run can manually confirm the second 'WALK' line appears near the 90s mark without any further keypress in the log.

test_cases.title: (CRITICAL REGRESSION) RAILWAY_PREEMPTION does not deadlock the intersection - arterial keeps cycling, connector permanently suppressed

checks.description: L1's SUPERVISORY column flips NORMAL_OPERATION(3) -> RAILWAY_PREEMPTION(1) within ~1s of RL1's first TRAIN_APPROACHING
arterial continues its own 48s green even though RAILWAY_PREEMPTION is active - direct disproof of the historical bug where a bare 'break' froze fsm->phase at PHASE_ALL_RED_A_TO_B forever

checks.pattern: Lx 1: SIGNAL -> ALL RED \(A to B\)
checks.description: yellow completes normally

CRITICAL: ALL_RED_A_TO_B must transition BACK to ARTERIAL_GREEN (not freeze, and not to CONNECTOR_GREEN) because supervisory==RAILWAY_PREEMPTION - this is the exact fix under regression test. The repeated RL1 direction-alternating presses (every 15s from t=20000 to t=95000) keep re-registering occupancy windows so the crossing stays closed well past this first cycle, proving the arterial loop keeps running rather than the crossing reopening and masking the bug.
SUPERVISORY must still read RAILWAY_PREEMPTION(1) at t~=100s given the repeated train pulses - confirms it never silently reverted to NORMAL_OPERATION mid-sequence

test_cases._note_for_reviewer: Proving 'more than one full 54s arterial cycle' strictly (i.e. a second, distinct ARTERIAL_GREEN recurrence at ~t=109s) is not expressible with this runner: a check for the same pattern text ('SIGNAL -> ARTERIAL GREEN') is satisfied by the FIRST post-t0 occurrence (~55s) regardless of within_ms, so it cannot selectively target a later recurrence. The checks above instead prove the core regression signature (transitions out of ALL_RED_A_TO_B back to ARTERIAL_GREEN, not frozen, not diverted to CONNECTOR_GREEN) plus that SUPERVISORY is still RAILWAY_PREEMPTION at t=100s (i.e. crossing still closed, so an operator/log reviewer inspecting results/TC-SC03A-1/L1.log can independently count further ARTERIAL YELLOW/GREEN recurrences beyond what the automated regex checks can individually distinguish). CONNECTOR GREEN must never appear at all during this window - this tool cannot assert an absence, so that specific invariant ("never CONNECTOR GREEN while RAILWAY_PREEMPTION active") is documented here for a human/log reviewer to confirm from the saved transcript rather than asserted by a check.

test_cases.title: (Critical regression, CC-03) drain-phase granted exactly once per railway reopening, +4s increments, 60s cap

checks.description: RAILWAY_PREEMPTION active with queue_warning_active=1 already set
single train reopens at ~51s (WARNING5+CLOSING3+ARRIVAL20+OCCUPANCY20+OPENING3)
drain_pending set on CROSSING_OPEN; L1's own ALL_RED_A_TO_B boundary (~54s from L1 boot) then enters CONNECTOR_GREEN with drain_active=1

base 30s (LX_PEAK_CONNECTOR_GREEN_MS) + full 60s drain cap (LX_DRAIN_MAX_EXTENSION_MS, 15 x 4s increments, queue_warning_active never cleared) = 90s total, so CONNECTOR_GREEN must end at ~54000+90000=144000ms - CRITICAL: must NOT keep extending past the 60s cap even though queue_warning_active is still 1
normal ALL_RED_B_TO_A(2s) follows the drain-extended CONNECTOR_YELLOW(4s) - confirms the FSM resumed ordinary cycling after the drain ended, at ~146000ms

test_cases._note_for_reviewer: The doc's 'exactly once per reopening' claim additionally requires proving the SECOND connector green after this (reached without any further RAILWAY_PREEMPTION cycle) lasts a normal undrained 30s. This tool's checks match the FIRST post-t0 occurrence of a given pattern regardless of within_ms, so a second check for 'CONNECTOR YELLOW' cannot selectively target the second occurrence (~t=230s) without also being trivially satisfied by the first occurrence already confirmed above at ~144s - the runner has no per-check custom time-window/since-offset field to express this. A reviewer can confirm the no-double-dip invariant by inspecting the timestamps of the two 'CONNECTOR YELLOW' lines in results/TC-SC03A-7/L1.log after a run with cleanup_wait_ms/checks extended further (second CONNECTOR_GREEN expected ~148500+48000+4000+2000=202500ms, second CONNECTOR_YELLOW expected at ~232500ms if truly undrained).

REGRESSION FINDING (this test-plan doc's stated known gap is now resolved by the newer 'r' demo key): pressing '0' again at t=15200ms while still RLX_CLOSED re-enters the RLX_CLOSED case of rlx_fsm_simulate_train_approaching(), which calls check_gate_contradiction_closed() - since gates_confirmed_closed() is now false (forced open by 'r'), this immediately raises FAULT_GATE_CONFIRM_MISSING. test_cases.title: PA-07: exactly 3 consecutive missed heartbeats before UNAVAILABLE
test_cases.skip_reason: Requires kill -STOP <pid lx_main 1> to stop its 1Hz heartbeat thread entirely (then kill -CONT to clean up) while observing C1's 1Hz-refreshed AVAILABILITY column tick-by-tick. This tool's schema only supports scripted stdin keystrokes to already-running subprocesses - there is no step type for sending OS signals to a node's pid, and no keystroke exists to make a running lx_main stop sending heartbeats without actually pausing the process, so this case cannot be driven through this harness.

test_cases.title: Resync on heartbeat recovery - instant AVAILABLE, and the RESYNCHRONISING display known gap
test_cases.skip_reason: This case's precondition is TC-SC05-1's UNAVAILABLE state, which itself requires kill -STOP/-CONT against the lx_main process (no stdin-only path exists to stop a running node's heartbeat). Since this tool's schema has no step type for sending OS signals to a node's pid, TC-SC05-1 is skipped and this dependent case is skipped for the same reason. (Separately, the doc's own 'Known gap' half of this case - that link_state is hard-coded LINK_CENTRAL_CONNECTED in every outgoing heartbeat/status payload in lx_comm.c/rlx_comm.c, so no RESYNCHRONISING state is ever genuinely observable - is a source-level limitation, not a test-automation one; it would remain true even with signal-sending support.)
